newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela's CANTV makes strong Wall Street debut.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's CANTV makes strong Wall Street debut.

text.p: Venezuelan telephone company CANTV made a $1.1 billion Wall Street splash Friday in one of Latin America's biggest public stock offerings in years.

CANTV's U.S. shares, known as American Depository Receipts (ADRs), jumped $2.875 to $25.875 as the Venezuelan government sold most of its remaining 49 percent stake in the company. The shares were the most heavily traded on the New York Stock Exchange, with 12.3 million traded.
Venezuelan officials hailed the buying as a sign of international confidence in President Rafael Caldera's reforms aimed at stabilising the economy of the oil-rich South American country.

"Today, this has been confirmed -- Venezuela and the government of Venezuela are strongly maintaining their resolution to keep the new economic policy on track," Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar told reporters.
Matos announced Venezuela would take a further step in its privatisation programme by selling Banco de Venezuela and Banco Consolidado on Dec. 18.

CANTV was the latest in a series of international telecommunications offerings to draw heavy interest on the NYSE. In recent weeks, Russia's Vimpel-Communications and Germany's Deutsche Telekom also have seen their initial public offerings snapped up by investors.

H. Nicholas Willward, managing director of capital markets at SBC Warburg, one of the issue's underwriters, said the issue was oversubscribed by "well more" than the three times many Wall Street analysts had expected.
He put the total value of Friday's offering at about $1.1 billion, among the biggest since the $3 billion privatisation of Argentine oil company YPF in 1993.

Analysts said CANTV's popularity stemmed in large part from managers whose portfolios are linked to Venezuelan stock listings. They bought shares more to keep up with the increased capitalisation of Venezuelan stocks caused by the CANTV sale than from a desire for the stock itself.
CANTV's penetration rate of 11.5 lines per 100 people is in line with much of Latin America, and its telephone rates are below the region's average.
Lucia Skwarek, head of Latin American equities at UBS Securities, said the CANTV shares were especially popular among portfolio managers who want to increase their exposure in Venezuela.
"This bodes well for all the Venezuelan market for the next several weeks," she said. "Venezuela in general will become much more of a traders' market."

CANTV, an acronym for Compania Anonima Nacional Telefonos de Venezuela, put up a total of 289.4 million Class D shares, with 80 percent sold in New York and London. Each American Depository Receipt represents seven Class D shares.
GTE Corp. said it planned to buy $200 million worth of shares and boost its stake in CANTV to 26 percent from 20.4 percent.
